bio: Evan McAleer is a Visual Instructor at the Phantom Regiment drum and bugle corps. He resides in Baton Rouge, Louisiana where he serves as Assistant Band Director at Catholic High School. He marched with the Glassmen and Carolina Crown, later working as a Visual Staff member for the Blue Knights during the summers of 2013 and 2014. He earned a Bachelor of Music Education from Louisiana State University in 2012.

Jonathan Meader marched with the Blue Devils, aging out in 2005. He served on color guard staff for Bluecoats (2011), Blue Knights (2014), and Oregon Crusaders (2014), where he was also credited as choreographer. He was visual designer for Legends (2016).

Over 18 years in the marching arts, Caleb Brown taught at DCI drum corps including the Seattle Cascades, Troopers, Mandarins, and Colts through 2019. He began in winter guard in high school and performed with Aria Winter Guard at WGI World Championships in 2009. Brown is a director of Third Coast Independent, a World Class winter guard in Houston, Texas.
Lara Pitts was a member of the Louisiana Stars educational leadership team for the 2023 season, described as an experienced veteran staff member who accepted a new position within the team.

Louis Hellinger served as a choreographer on the Madison Scouts Color Guard Instructional Team for the 2018 season. He was part of the staff at AMP Winterguard, which had assumed the top guard position in New Jersey, and was discussed as a potential staff acquisition for The Cadets.

Reuben Rodriguez served as Audio Systems Designer for Phantom Regiment in 2023. He is an alumnus of Revolution, Crossmen, Spirit, and The Cavaliers Drum & Bugle Corps, and from 2017-2022 served as Audio Engineer to Caption Manager Coordinator for The Cavaliers. He also served as sound designer for Red Line Percussion and The Crossmen Drum & Bugle Corps.

Wesley Tyree is a color guard instructor and the Guard Director at Plano East Senior High School. He earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts in dance from The Ohio State University and marched with the Colts Drum and Bugle Corps. He has instructed for the Blue Stars Drum & Bugle Corps and has worked with numerous independent and scholastic color guard programs.
Ken Masaki served as an Audio Engineer for The Cavaliers during their 75th anniversary season in 2023.

Sarah Wagner is a DCI brass instructor who has taught the Battalion (2023 trumpets), Boston Crusaders (2022 mellophones), The Academy/Arizona Academy (2019-2021 high brass), and Oregon Crusaders (2017-2018 high brass), and currently serves as Brass Caption Head for the Troopers Legacy Corps (2026 is her seventh year). She holds dual Master's degrees in Trumpet Performance and Wind Conducting from the University of Denver and a Bachelor of Music Education from Colorado Mesa University, and is Director of Bands at Broomfield High School and Broomfield Heights Middle School in Colorado. She also performs with the Denver Broncos Stampede Drumline, Colorado Avalanche Celly Squad, Denver Nuggets Skyline Drumline, and is a charter member of the all-female Beauty and the Beats Drumline.

Turner Hawkins is a musician and educator from Lexington, Kentucky. He marched with the Madison Scouts and the Blue Devils, winning the 2015 DCI World Championship as a member of the Blue Devils. He has held drum corps brass teaching positions at the Oregon Crusaders, Blue Stars, and Concord Blue Devils.

Michael Terry performed as a member of The Cadets Drum and Bugle Corps from 2000 to 2007, was a featured soloist, and the corps won DCI World Championships in 2000 and 2005; he was twice named Cadet of the Year. He later served on the brass faculty for the Troopers (2010-2013), as Brass Co-Caption Head for Spirit of Atlanta (2014), and returned to The Cadets as brass staff teaching mellophones in 2015, winning Rookie Staff Member of the Year, and was announced as Brass Caption Head for 2017.

Michael Townsend served as color guard director for the Boston Crusaders, working alongside program coordinator Keith Potter and drill designer Leon May to produce shows for the corps. He and the design team had developed a working relationship spanning approximately eight years as of 2016.

Zach Schlicher began his drum corps career with The Cadets in 2001, serving as percussion section leader in his final season. After aging out in 2004, he taught snare line at the Madison Scouts (2005-2006) and then served on the faculty of Carolina Crown for ten years. In 2016 he joined the Boston Crusaders as Percussion Production Designer. He studied percussion at Indiana University of Pennsylvania and the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

Ben Harloff has taught drum corps since 1999, including The Cadets, Carolina Crown, and Bluecoats (as a Brass Consultant in 2022). He holds degrees from Indiana University (Trumpet Performance, Music Education) and a Master's in conducting from Southern Oregon University. He marched Star of Indiana from 1990 to 1993 and was a trumpet soloist in the Tony Award-winning show 'Blast!'.

Jeff Sacktig is a DCI and WGI Hall of Fame visual designer and educator. He marched with the Cadets from 1986 to 1989, served on their visual staff through 1994, and was their drill designer from 1995 to 2015. He returned to drum corps in 2017 with Carolina Crown. He has also designed for numerous WGI groups including Dartmouth Indoor Percussion, United Percussion, and Paramount.

Jonathan Yoo is the Audio Caption Supervisor at Carolina Crown Drum and Bugle Corps, providing Electronics and Sound Design, Show Design, and Visual Design. His DCI teaching experience includes Pacific Crest, Santa Clara Vanguard, Glassmen, Spirit of Atlanta, Music City, and Carolina Crown. He marched as a performer with the Madison Scouts Drum and Bugle Corps and is a WGI Percussion Visual Effect Judge.

Michael Klesch began his drum corps career in the early 1980s as a performer with the Garfield Cadets, becoming drum major in 1983 and brass caption supervisor and arranger by age 23. He has served as music director and brass arranger for Carolina Crown since 2003 and was inducted into the DCI Hall of Fame in 2012. Klesch has worked with numerous corps including Phantom Regiment, Spirit of Atlanta, Colts, Crossmen, Troopers, The Academy, and others.

Tom Rarick is the Director of Percussion and a designer for the Bluecoats Drum & Bugle Corps, having served as their percussion arranger/composer since 2009 after previously holding the role of front ensemble arranger since 2002. He was previously a marching and staff member with the Cadets of Bergen County. He is a percussionist with the United States Air Force Band Ceremonial Brass, a position he has held since 1997. He is a signature artist for Innovative Percussion and endorses Evans Drumheads, Tama | Bergerault, and Zildjian.

Andrew Ricketts joined the Boston Crusaders percussion staff in 2017 after six seasons as a bass drum and battery instructor for The Cadets (2013–2016). He previously marched with The Cadets (2011–2012) and The Raiders (2008–2009), and has taught with Jersey Surf Drum & Bugle Corps. Ricketts holds a bachelor's degree in Psychology from UMass Amherst and has performed as a drummer at the DCI World Championship with The Cadets.

Andy Toth was a member of the design team and choreographer for The Cavaliers Drum & Bugle Corps from 1998-2015 and joined Santa Clara Vanguard as Visual Coordinator and Choreographer in 2017. He performed as an original cast member of the Emmy and Tony award-winning production of Blast! in London's West End (1999) and on Broadway until 2001. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Exercise Physiology from the University of Illinois at Chicago and has served on the WGI Steering Committee since 2016.

Brian Franco-Winn (Brian Winn) is an Assistant Professor of Dance at Winthrop University who directs and choreographs for color guard programs nationwide. He serves as Color Guard Choreographer for Carolina Crown and is an active choreographer, clinician, and adjudicator in the pageantry arts community. He also serves as director of Etude and sits on the Advisory Boards for the Carolina Winter Ensemble Association and Winter Guard International.

Daniel Riley has served as the Color Guard Caption Head for the Santa Clara Vanguard since 2013. He was part of two DCI World Championship victories with The Cadets (2000 and 2011) and a DCI World Championship in 2018 with the Santa Clara Vanguard. Riley also worked with Northmont High School, Braddock Independent, and Paramount Winter Guard among other groups.

Eric Shriver is a percussion educator, composer, and arranger based in Southern California. He currently serves as Percussion Director and Battery Arranger for Pacific Crest Drum & Bugle Corps, and has previously held percussion caption head and battery arranger roles with the Blue Stars and Gold drum corps, and served as a snare technician for the Bluecoats and The Cavaliers. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Music (Industry Studies) from California Polytechnic University, Pomona, and is the creator of "The Build-Up Method" percussion practice system.

James Ancona has more than 30 years of experience as a composer and instructor for world-class drum and bugle corps. He is currently a percussion advisor for the Boston Crusaders and has served on the instructional staff of The Cadets and Carolina Crown, among other corps. He was a member of the 1990 DCI World Champion Cadets of Bergen County and served as Percussion Caption Head for the 2006 DCI World Champion Cavaliers.

Jared Kortz marched with the Glassmen (2008–2009) and aged out at Phantom Regiment (2010), winning the DCI Fred Sanford Award for High Percussion. He was a bass technician for the Crossmen (2012–2013, 2015–2018) and has served on the percussion staff of the Bluecoats. He is also an educator at Rhythm X and an Innovative Percussion Education Artist.

Jay Bocook served as chief arranger for the Cadets Drum and Bugle Corps from 1993-2023 and has arranged for the Blue Knights Drum and Bugle Corps. He became brass arranger for The Cavaliers beginning with the 2025 season. He was inducted into the Drum Corps International Hall of Fame in 2009 and serves as Director of Athletic Bands at Furman University.

Chris Carrasco is a designer, choreographer, and teacher who joined the Troopers design team in 2019. He works as a visual technician for the Blue Devils and as program coordinator and drill designer for Blue Devils B, and previously served as a movement specialist and choreographer for Santa Clara Vanguard. He has also been a choreographer for the Madison Scouts and Yokohama Scouts, and is the Associate Director of Bands at James Logan High School.

Doug Thrower started his drum corps career at age 11 with the Krescendos from Peterborough, Ontario, and later marched with the Seneca Optimists. He worked as a brass instructor and arranger for Canadian corps including the Canadian Knights, Kiwanis Kavaliers, Cardinals, and Dutch Boy before joining the Bluecoats in 1992 as a brass instructor, becoming brass caption head in 1993 and adding arranging duties in 1997. He is credited with creating the viral "pitch bend" effect in Bluecoats' 2014 production _Tilt_ and his arranging was central to the corps' first DCI World Championship in 2016. Thrower was inducted into the DCI Hall of Fame in 2019 and the Bluecoats Hall of Fame in 2009.

Ian Hale is a percussion educator who has served on the percussion staff for the Madison Scouts, Carolina Crown, The Cadets, and currently the Boston Crusaders Drum and Bugle Corps. He holds a BA in percussion performance from the University of Calgary and an MA from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and has also taught percussion for the Glassmen and the Magic of Orlando.

Rafael Bretado began his drum corps career with the Velvet Knights B-Line cymbal line in 1994 and marched with the Santa Clara Vanguard cymbal line from 1996 to 1998. He served as a cymbal technician for Santa Clara Vanguard from 2011 onward and as corps director of the Vanguard Cadets. He is a native Californian.

Ryan George is a composer and arranger who served as brass arranger/composer for the Boston Crusaders (8th year as of 2023) and also worked with the Academy Drum & Bugle Corps. He resides in Austin, Texas and is a graduate of the University of Kentucky. His concert and marching works have been performed at Carnegie Hall, PASIC, the Midwest Clinic, and by the U.S. Marine Band.

Seth Murphy has over 20 years of experience in the marching arts, beginning as a brass musician with Carolina Crown and later serving on the brass faculty there. He held brass caption management roles at Pacific Crest, Blue Stars, and The Cadets, served as a brass consultant for the Mandarins, and worked with Santa Clara Vanguard in 2024 as a Brass Ensemble Specialist. He earned a Bachelor's Degree in Music Performance from Winthrop University and performed with the Tony and Emmy Award-winning production Blast!.

Aaron Barnes marched with The Cadets (2002–2003) and began his marching career with the Reading Buccaneers (2001). He has served as Co-Caption Head for the Blue Stars, Caption Supervisor for the Crossmen, and worked with Jersey Surf and Boston Crusaders. He was on the educational staff at The Cadets, contributing to a DCI World Championship and the John Brazale Best Visual Performance award.

Bill Fritz is the Staff Director and Brass Caption Head of Gold Drum and Bugle Corps. He has taught at Pacific Crest Drum & Bugle Corps and Academy Drum & Bugle Corps, and performed with Pacific Crest and as a member of the 2007 World Champion Blue Devils. He holds a BA in Music Education, a BM in saxophone performance, and a Master's in Instrumental Conducting from California State University, Fullerton.

Brad Green (Brad Kerr Green) has served as a brass instructor, brass caption head, brass caption supervisor, and brass arranger/composer for drum and bugle corps including the Blue Knights, Santa Clara Vanguard, Blue Stars, Madison Scouts, and Oregon Crusaders. He began his drum corps career as a euphonium player for the Cadets of Bergen County in 1995 and aged-out as Drum Major for the Cadets in 1998, earning the Jim Jones Leadership award. He holds a BA from The New School and a Master's from Troy University, and is a composer and arranger for the United States Air Force band.

Dan Schack is a designer, educator, clinician, and adjudicator in the marching arts. He serves as Battery Coordinator for the Bluecoats Drum & Bugle Corps and Program Coordinator & Battery Arranger for the Connecticut Hurricanes Drum and Bugle Corps. He also serves as Creative Director & Battery Caption Head of the George Mason University Indoor Drumline.

James Rocillo has served on the brass staff of the Blue Devils A Corps since 2008, contributing to nine DCI Championships and earning four Jim Ott Awards for outstanding brass performance. He is the Program Designer and Creative Director for Gold Drum & Bugle Corps. Rocillo is also an Associate Professor at Riverside City College, directing the Marching Tigers, jazz ensemble, and concert band.

Jared Andrews is a percussion educator currently serving as Battery Caption Supervisor at Carolina Crown. He served on percussion staff for the Blue Devils from 2012 to 2017 and was a battery percussion consultant for the Madison Scouts in 2022.
John Lluvera is a marching arts professional based in Clearwater, Florida. He has been associated with the Bluecoats Drum and Bugle Corps and is listed as an artist on Pearl Drums.

John Max McFarland has been the Program Coordinator for Legends Drum and Bugle Corps since 2016 and was the percussion composer/arranger for Pioneer Drum and Bugle Corps from 2013 to 2015. He also served as percussion caption head and arranger for the Erie Thunderbirds in 2018 and was a marching member of the Kiwanis Kavaliers and Santa Clara Vanguard. He is an active composer/arranger in WGI, DCI, and BOA.

Jonathan Leal is a percussion educator who has been part of the Santa Clara Vanguard percussion education team since 2013, and previously taught the Boston Crusaders Drum and Bugle Corps. He performed with the Santa Clara Vanguard, Phantom Regiment, and Revolution drum corps, as well as the University of North Texas Indoor Drumline. He holds a PhD in Modern Thought & Literature from Stanford University and teaches at the University of Southern California.

Kevin LeBoeuf is a marching arts producer and brass educator who has served as Brass Caption Head for the Bluecoats Drum & Bugle Corps since 2023, leading the corps to its first Jim Ott Memorial Brass Award in 2024 and a perfect 100 in achievement at the 2025 finals. He previously served as Brass Caption Manager for The Cavaliers (2018-2022) and on the Carolina Crown brass staff (2015-2017). In 2025 he joined the Bluecoats Design Team as a Music Designer while continuing as Brass Caption Head. He holds a degree in Music Education from Rutgers University and a graduate degree in wind-band conducting from UCLA, and also serves as Brass Caption Head for the Aimachi marching band in Japan.

Lee Allman is a freelance music educator and arranger who serves as Percussion Director at Avon High School and front ensemble arranger for The Cavaliers. He is Assistant Percussion Caption Head at the Crossmen and has previously taught with the Troopers and Carolina Crown. He holds a Bachelor of Music in Percussion Performance from the Jacobs School of Music at Indiana University.

Mike Bishop is a producer, composer, arranger, sound designer, and music educator from Philadelphia who serves as the sound designer for Carolina Crown. He has designed or served on the education faculty for Carolina Crown, Crossmen, Blue Stars, United Percussion, and Rhythm X, among other groups. He is a signed Yamaha, Zildjian, Vic Firth, and Remo artist and graduated Summa Cum Laude as valedictorian from Full Sail University.

Mike Jackson has been teaching, composing, and designing percussion programs for over three decades. He marched with Velvet Knights, Suncoast Sound, and the Blue Knights, and has worked with drum corps including Santa Clara Vanguard, Bluecoats, Blue Knights, and Carolina Crown (percussion designer, 2023). He was inducted into the WGI Hall of Fame in 2010.

Mike Scott is the Chief Executive Officer of the Bluecoats drum and bugle corps. He works with EN-RICH-MENT on its percussion programs, providing advice on training, equipment, and performance opportunities. He manages more than 200 young adults annually and helped lead the Bluecoats to a world championship. He holds a Bachelor of Music with a minor in business from Miami University (2012).
